assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a genuinely new class of quantum matter, protected by band topology rather than symmetry breaking. The idea (Z2 invariant, helical edge states) is original, conceptually clean and has reshaped condensed-matter physics and materials search.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction and Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive HgTe quantum spin Hall measurement following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The credited triple is a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, though the 3D topological insulator work (not credited here) and the BHZ proposal are left out.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of independent confirmation in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and ARPES-measured 3D materials, with theory and spectroscopy in agreement. Timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and 3D topological insulators lies outside the credited names.
Whether Mele or Molenkamp is the better third laureate is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed flat bands with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable, clean system. It is a striking case of experiment overturning expectations and has created a whole field (moire materials).
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. Credit fits a theory-plus-experiment pair, with Bistritzer's role potentially subordinate to MacDonald's.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced by many groups, with STM, transport and spectroscopy agreement. The microscopic origin of superconductivity and the full phase diagram remain debated, so interpretation is still maturing, but the core discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and some correlated-phase interpretations remain unsettled.
Possible competing credit to other experimental groups and to the theory of Lopes dos Santos et al. and Suarez Morell et al., not in the supplied names.
Whether two or three laureates is appropriate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the leading quantitative framework for strongly correlated electrons, bridging band theory and many-body physics. It explains Mott transitions and, combined with DFT, predicts spectra of real correlated materials, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar built the DMFT mapping onto the Anderson impurity model, and Vollhardt (with Metzner) established the infinite-dimension limit. The credited triple is plausible, but Walter Metzner is missing from the supplied names, which is a real attribution gap.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use, benchmarked against experimental photoemission and thermodynamic data and extended by DFT+DMFT. Very mature; the question is whether a theory method fits the prize better than a discovery.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner from the credited names.
A methods prize may be seen as less of a physical discovery than the committee prefers.
Systematic limits for low-dimensional systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductors was a surprise, as a magnetic element was not expected to host high-Tc pairing. It opened a second family of unconventional superconductors with a rich magnetism-superconductivity interplay.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's 2008 LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx report is the clear originating discovery, so a single laureate is straightforward. Subsequent rapid Tc increases by Chinese groups and the theoretical pairing proposals are not credited in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced within weeks and extensively characterised by neutron, ARPES and DFT studies. The pairing mechanism is still debated, but the discovery is firmly established.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity remains unresolved.
Sole credit may be contested by those who raised Tc and by theorists of s-plus-minus pairing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the giant MgO-based enhancement underpin magnetic sensors and MRAM. It builds on the spin-dependent tunnelling physics and extends the 2007 GMR prize, with strong DFT understanding of coherent tunnelling.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's group and others demonstrated large MgO-based TMR. Julliere's early work and the Yuasa/Djayaprawira contributions complicate a clean three-person credit.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and technologically deployed; the coherent-tunnelling theory is well tested against first-principles calculations. Recognition is timely but may be viewed as incremental after GMR.
uncertainties: Credit for MgO-based coherent tunnelling (Yuasa, Parkin, Butler, Mathon) is dispersed.
Possible overlap with the 2007 prize scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED realised strong light-matter coupling on a chip and is the architecture for superconducting qubits, linking to the 2025 prize's circuit quantum physics. It is original and underpins current quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators proposed the architecture; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. A natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, with Schoelkopf's later transmon and readout work also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed across many labs and platforms. Timing is sensitive: the committee recently recognised superconducting-circuit physics, which could weigh against another circuit-related prize soon.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may reduce appetite.
Credit also due to Devoret, Nakamura and others on related circuit physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials and PAW made large-scale first-principles calculations of real materials routine, so that DFT predictions of magnetism, structure and spectra became quantitative and reproducible. Its impact on materials science is vast, though the Nobel framing is methodological.
assessment.attribution: Vanderbilt introduced ultrasoft pseudopotentials, Blöchl the PAW method, and Kresse the VASP implementation that made it widely usable. A fair triple, though the scientific line from Phillips, Kleinman, Bylander and others is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Used in thousands of studies and benchmarked across codes (as in the Science 2016 reproducibility study). Mature, but a methods and software prize may fall outside a discovery-centred preference, and the 1998 Chemistry prize already recognised DFT.
uncertainties: Whether the physics prize should recognise computational methods.
Overlap with the 1998 DFT Chemistry prize.
Attribution of Kresse as implementation versus method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock achieves unprecedented fractional frequency stability and is poised to redefine the second and enable tests of fundamental physics. The magic-wavelength idea is original and elegant, with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group pushed it to record accuracy and many-body clock physics. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though other groups (Lemonde, Bloom) also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent clocks agree at the 1e-18 level, and the redefinition of the second is under consideration. Mature, though the 2005 prize recognised related precision spectroscopy; this is outside my core field so I defer to AMO colleagues.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 Hall and Hansch prize scope.
Other credited groups, such as Lemonde or Ludlow and Bloom, are not in the supplied names.
I defer to AMO members on relative merit.
